16	package org.springframework.samples.petclinic.util;
17	
18	import java.util.Map;
19	
20	/**
21	 * Single source of truth for the fixed region-to-timezone table ({@code NSW->Australia/Sydney,
22	 * VIC->Australia/Melbourne, QLD->Australia/Brisbane}). The owner's derived read-only
23	 * {@code timezone} ({@code OwnerMapper}) consults this one table, so a region added or renamed
24	 * here is reflected everywhere at once.
25	 */
26	public final class RegionTimezones {
27	
28	    private static final Map<String, String> REGION_TIMEZONE = Map.of(
29	        "NSW", "Australia/Sydney", "VIC", "Australia/Melbourne", "QLD", "Australia/Brisbane");
30	
31	    private RegionTimezones() {
32	    }
33	
34	    /**
35	     * Return the IANA timezone name for {@code region}, or {@code null} when the region is not in
36	     * the fixed table.
37	     *
38	     * @param region the owner's region/locality (may be {@code null})
39	     * @return the IANA timezone (e.g. {@code "Australia/Sydney"}) or {@code null} when the region
40	     *         has no mapped timezone
41	     */
42	    public static String timezoneOf(String region) {
43	        return REGION_TIMEZONE.get(region);
44	    }
45	}

16	package org.springframework.samples.petclinic.util;
17	
18	import java.util.Map;
19	
20	/**
21	 * Single source of truth for the fixed city-to-region table ({@code Sydney->NSW, Melbourne->VIC,
22	 * Brisbane->QLD}). Both the owner's derived {@code locality} ({@code OwnerMapper}) and the postcode
23	 * range rule ({@link PostcodeRules}) consult this one table, so a city added or renamed here is
24	 * reflected everywhere at once.
25	 */
26	public final class CityRegions {
27	
28	    private static final Map<String, String> CITY_REGION = Map.of(
29	        "Sydney", "NSW", "Melbourne", "VIC", "Brisbane", "QLD");
30	
31	    private CityRegions() {
32	    }
33	
34	    /**
35	     * Return the canonical region for {@code city}, or {@code null} when the city is not in the
36	     * fixed table.
37	     *
38	     * @param city the owner's city (may be {@code null})
39	     * @return the region (e.g. {@code "NSW"}) or {@code null} when the city has no known region
40	     */
41	    public static String regionOf(String city) {
42	        return CITY_REGION.get(city);
43	    }
44	}

VERDICT: CHANGES REQUESTED

The logic placement is otherwise idiomatic — a `toOwnerSegment(Owner)` default method sitting alongside its `toX(owner)` siblings, wired through an `@Mapping(... expression)`, with a matching Javadoc and openapi schema. The tier/area composition is clear. One structural issue:

**The known-region set `{NSW, VIC, QLD}` is re-enumerated inline.** Line 116:

```java
boolean metro = "NSW".equals(locality) || "VIC".equals(locality) || "QLD".equals(locality);
```

This hardcodes a fourth parallel copy of the set of known regions. The codebase deliberately centralizes this knowledge and each holder documents it as the single source of truth so "a region added or renamed here is reflected everywhere at once":
- `CityRegions.CITY_REGION` (Sydney→NSW, Melbourne→VIC, Brisbane→QLD)
- `PostcodeRules.REGION_POSTCODES` (NSW/VIC/QLD ranges)
- `RegionTimezones.REGION_TIMEZONE` (NSW/VIC/QLD → timezone)

A new inline `equals` disjunction is exactly the scattered, drift-prone region knowledge this convention exists to prevent — add a region (say TAS) tomorrow and this one method silently keeps classifying it as `REGIONAL`, out of step with `locality` and `timezone`.

Suggested fixes (either is in keeping with the surrounding code):
- Simplest: `toLocality` already collapses every non-known region to the `"UNKNOWN"` sentinel, so the membership test can lean on that single resolution point rather than re-listing the regions:
  ```java
  boolean metro = !"UNKNOWN".equals(locality);
  ```
- Or, if an explicit membership predicate reads better, source it from a shared table — e.g. a `RegionTimezones.isKnownRegion(locality)` (a region with a mapped timezone) or a dedicated known-regions set — so the "known region" set stays defined in one place, consistent with the three utilities above.
